source.title: AOGNets: Compositional Grammatical Architectures for Deep Learning
source.authors: Xi-Lai Li; Xi Song; Tianfu Wu

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates architecture performance and a general network-dissection interpretability metric, but does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or measure polysemanticity.
record.gate_note: The paper reports classification and adversarial-robustness results, which do not measure the claim. It also reports a network-dissection interpretability comparison; this is recorded as a related but different measure under fits_no_version. The paper's discussion of interpretability does not assess whether individual neurons have coherent or mixed meanings.
record.test_reason: An architecture paper (AOGNets) reporting classification, detection, and adversarial-robustness results. Its only interpretability result is a network-dissection count of unique detectors in the last conv layer (Fig. 6). That count does not measure whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so no version is tested. Polysemanticity is never mentioned, so 'discusses' applies only loosely, to interpretability in general.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that AOGNets outperform the compared networks on accuracy and get the best network-dissection interpretability score. They also say AOGNets show better potential for adversarial defense.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses network dissection to compare detector counts, not a method for identifying or testing polysemantic neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: In the last conv layer, AOGNets have more unique network-dissection detectors than the other ImageNet networks compared (Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture choice changes the number of unique concept detectors identified by network dissection.

record.problems: The network-dissection comparison is presented in a figure without exact values in the text; the paper reports no uncertainty for this comparison. Its detector-count metric does not directly measure polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Classification benchmark, object detection/segmentation, and adversarial-attack results are not rows because they do not measure neuron polysemanticity or its proposed causes.

untested.parts: No individual neuron's responses to multiple unrelated image inputs are examined.
No superposition, feature sparsity or capacity analysis.
No analysis of initialization, regularization or noise as causes of polysemanticity.
Architectures are compared, but only on unique-detector counts, not on the share of polysemantic neurons.
No canonical polysemantic neurons are re-examined.
No variation in activation range or explanation scoring is examined.

record.verdict_notes: The paper never mentions polysemantic neurons or superposition. Network dissection is used only as a summary interpretability score, with no per-neuron analysis of mixed selectivity.

versions.untested_parts: No individual-neuron responses to image inputs or neuron meanings are measured.
No transformer language models, MLP neurons, or token/context responses are studied.
No feature sparsity, capacity pressure, or superposition is measured.
No polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise is measured.
Architectures are compared using network dissection, but the share of polysemantic neurons and its relation to architecture, activation, regularization, or performance is not measured.
No canonical mixed-response neurons are examined to determine whether they share a feature or related job.
No variation in activation range or explanation-scoring method for polysemanticity is examined.

rows.subject: AOGNet (models summarized collectively in the text)
rows.operation_detail: Compared network-dissection detector counts in the last convolution layer.

conditions.value: ImageNet-pretrained networks; includes AOGNets and other architectures shown in Figure 6
number of unique detectors and number of detectors by category

rows.measure: Network-dissection interpretability score based on detector counts.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Figure 6, and accompanying Results and Analyses text
rows.note: The text states that AOGNet obtains the best score in the comparison. Figure 6 plots detector counts, but exact values are not stated in the text. This metric does not establish whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: The detector-count metric cannot show whether units are polysemantic, so 'observed' has no meaning for any version. The subject is several ImageNet-pretrained networks (AOGNets, ResNets, DenseNet, GoogLeNet, VGG, AlexNet), not AOGNet alone. Values are figure-only.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
